\newcommand{\Conclusion}{RQ1: memory-poisoning attacks causally change a 7B agent's behaviour (net +43.2 [39.5, 46.8] points), but which instances count as working depends on the probe and judge; defense rankings do not. RQ2: provenance-aware admission works through corroboration against the owner's own conversation, not through channel trust; it survives a real memory system's extraction (Mem0 stored the poisoned claim in 155/157 cases and corroboration still excluded 59/157 at 37/262 benign), leaves user-channel poisoning untouched, and its operating point depends on the calibration owners. Natural retrieval, not admission, was the first filter: only 48/157 stored poisons reached the agent for their task. RQ3: consolidation launders excluded poisons and lineage-taint containment decays from the first to the second generation, holding only through inherited state. RQ4: conditional memories are dormant and trigger-activated; content detection catches explicit rules in raw form but only 22/60 once Mem0 has reworded them and none of the implicit rules (0/60), and no sleeper-specific detector works. None of the three gaps is solved; the evidence supports evaluating defenses on attacks shown to work, through real memory pipelines, with benign lookalikes and owner-specific evidence.}

\newcommand{\MemAbstract}{Through Mem0 with its LLM extraction enabled, 155/157 hold-out-4 attacks left a stored memory carrying their claim, 48/157 were retrieved, and 29/157 changed the agent's answer; corroboration on what Mem0 stored excluded 59/157 attacks and 37/262 benign notes.}
\newcommand{\MemBody}{We repeated hold-out~4 (clean owner) and SA-1 through Mem0~2.0.19 with \texttt{infer=True}: the owner's first 100 turns were ingested naturally and each item was then ingested naturally into an isolated copy of that store, arriving either as text the assistant read from a shared document (untrusted) or as the user's own message. Defenses ran on what Mem0 \emph{stored}; the agent answered from Mem0's own top-5 retrieval, against a control store without the item. \textbf{Hold-out 4 (document channel).} Of 157 attacks, 157/157 produced a stored memory, 155/157 carried the note's claim (M1-1~HELD), 48/157 were retrieved for their probe (M1-5~FAILED), and 29/157 changed the answer relative to the control. On the stored memories, B12 excluded 2/157, B13 without corroboration 2/157 and B13 59/157 (M1-2~HELD, M1-3~HELD); of benign notes B13 excluded 37/262 (M1-4~HELD). Pipeline-working attacks fell from 29/157 to 16/157 under B13 (M1-6~HELD). On the raw notes our recomputation reproduces the published B13 decisions (item for item). Through the user channel, 155/157 attacks were stored and 29/157 changed the answer; B13 excludes none there by design. \textbf{SA-1.} Through the document channel, 58 of 60 conditional backdoors and 47 of 60 benign rules were stored at all; 10/60 attacks kept a conditional form (M2-3~HELD). The trigger retrieved the stored rule in 55/60 cases, yet attacks activated on only 7/60 triggers (and 0/60 unrelated messages; M2-1~HELD, M2-2~HELD): Mem0's rewording largely defused the rules. B12 on the stored memories excluded 22/60 attacks and 1/60 benign rules, against 60/60 attacks on the raw notes (M2-4~HELD, M2-5~HELD): extraction removed the explicit wording that content detection relied on, leaving 1/60 trigger activations. These results establish pipeline behaviour for these two corpora through one memory system only.}

\newcommand{\PtwoAbstract}{carried the payload into a second consolidation in 98/249 instances; containing those second-generation summaries depends on inheriting the intermediate summary's state (withheld carrying summaries: 24/71 with inheritance, 0/71 without).}
\newcommand{\PtwoBody}{Second-generation summaries carried the poison's payload in 98/249 instances (95/148 of those whose first summary carried it; P2-1~HELD). Serving them on B13-excluded instances produced harm in 22/161 (P2-4~HELD). Of the 71 carrying summaries of excluded poisons, containment withheld 0/71 (lexical), 24/71 (semantic, inheriting the parent's state), 24/71 (adding grandparents) and 0/71 (grandparents only, no inheritance; P2-3~HELD); P2-2~HELD. The semantic inheriting arm also withheld 7/90 summaries that did not carry the payload (P2-5~FAILED) and 4/79 benign chains. Harm with each arm: A0 22/161, L-inh 22/161, S-inh 13/161, S-inh+d2 13/161, S-noinh 22/161. No arm acts on the 88 instances admission missed, 27 of whose second summaries still carry the payload.}
\newcommand{\RemHolm}{Holm-adjusted $p$: SA-2 9.5e-07; SA-3 2.5e-30; SA-5 9.5e-07; SA-8 7.6e-06; P2-2 6.0e-07; P2-4 9.5e-07. Gap-closure family (MEM-1, MEM-2, SA-2): \GapHolm{}.}
\newcommand{\SAoneAbstract}{a pre-registered experiment with 60 conditional backdoors and 60 benign conditional lookalikes found activation on a natural trigger in 23/60 attacks and on an unrelated message in 0/60; admission-time content detection excluded 60/60 attacks and 2/60 lookalikes before activation---because these backdoors state their malicious action explicitly, not because any sleeper-specific signal worked (a dedicated sleeper guard flagged 0/60).}
\newcommand{\SAoneBody}{Each of 60 conditional backdoors and 60 benign conditional lookalikes (same author, owner, prompt and third-person syntax) carries a natural trigger message and an unrelated message. The note was retrieved into the agent's top five by its trigger in 51/60 attacks and 38/60 lookalikes, and by the unrelated message in 4/60 and 3/60. Undefended, attacks activated (complied with the note present, not without it) on 23/60 trigger messages and 0/60 unrelated messages (SA-1~HELD, dormancy; SA-2~HELD, paired +23/$-$0, $p$=2.4e-07); under the human-calibrated vote judge, 42/60 and 1/60. Lookalikes, whose activation is the intended behaviour, activated on 9/60 triggers. At admission, before any activation, B13 on the untrusted channel excluded 60/60 attacks and 3/60 lookalikes (SA-3~HELD, Fisher $p$=4.1e-31); B12 60 and 2 (SA-4~HELD). B13 reduced trigger activation from 23/60 to 0/60 (SA-5~HELD, $p$=2.4e-07) and lookalike activation from 9/60 to 8/60. On the user channel B13 excluded 0 attacks, by construction. The dedicated Phase~8 sleeper guard flagged 0/60 attacks (SA-6~HELD); the development-fitted anomaly signal flagged 60/60 attacks and 60/60 lookalikes (SA-7~HELD); deberta flagged 8/60 and 2/60. At activation time, the instruction-aware frame changed attack activation from 23/60 to 5/60 (SA-8~HELD, $p$=7.6e-06) and lookalike activation from 9/60 to 13/60 (SA-9~HELD). The interpretation matters: B12 alone excluded every attack, so detection here rests on the explicit payload (a named outside company and a covert action), not on dormancy; mundane, instruction-free sleeper notes are not caught by content detection (0\% on the project's sleeper family) and only partly by corroboration. B13's corroboration thresholds were calibrated on this owner's conversation among others (\S\ref{sec:limits}).}
\newcommand{\SAtwoBody}{The note was retrieved by its trigger in 50/60 attacks and by the unrelated message in 3/60; attacks activated on 33/60 triggers and 0/60 unrelated messages (S2-4a~HELD, S2-4b~HELD; vote judge 23/60 on triggers). Content-only B12 excluded 0/60 attacks and 0/60 benign rules (S2-1~HELD, S2-2~HELD); deberta 0/60; the Phase~8 sleeper guard 0/60 (S2-5~HELD); the development-fitted anomaly signal flagged 59/60 attacks and 60/60 benign rules. B13's corroboration excluded 40/60 attacks and 0/60 benign rules (S2-3~HELD, Fisher $p$=3.7e-17) and reduced trigger activation from 33/60 to 12/60. Because the benign rules were written to reflect what the owner said, corroboration's clean separation is partly by construction; the robust finding is the negative one: no content, injection or sleeper-specific detector recognised implicit conditional poisoning, and only owner-specific evidence did.}
